This operation provides comprehensive search functionality for system administrators to locate and review configuration settings across the platform. It supports filtering by configuration key patterns, functional categories, data types, and sensitivity flags, enabling precise targeting of specific configuration groups.

Results are paginated with configurable page sizes to handle large configuration sets efficiently. Each result includes the configuration key, value, data type, category, and description for quick review and management.

operations.description:
Permanently removes a system configuration record from the discussion board platform using soft deletion.

This operation deactivates a specific system configuration identified by its unique identifier by setting the deleted_at timestamp. System configurations control various platform behaviors including rate limits, content policies, display settings, and feature toggles. When a configuration is soft-deleted, it remains in the database with the deleted_at timestamp set but is no longer active in the system.

Administrators should exercise caution when deleting system configurations as this action affects platform functionality. The deletion process includes validation to ensure the configuration exists and proper authorization checks to prevent unauthorized modifications to critical system settings.

This operation implements soft deletion, preserving the configuration record in the database for audit and recovery purposes. The configuration can be restored by clearing the deleted_at field if needed. For complete removal from the database, database-level operations would be required.

Related operations include GET /system-configurations/{configurationId} for viewing configuration details and PATCH /system-configurations for listing and searching configurations.

operations.description:
Create a new maintenance schedule for system maintenance activities.

This operation allows administrators to schedule planned maintenance windows for the discussion board platform. Maintenance schedules include comprehensive details about the type of maintenance, expected duration, impact level, and responsible administrators.

When creating a maintenance schedule, administrators must provide essential information including the maintenance type (system update, database backup, security patch, etc.), detailed description of the activity, scheduled start and end times, estimated duration, and impact assessment. The system validates that scheduled times are in the future and that the scheduled end time occurs after the scheduled start time.

Maintenance schedules employ logical deletion capabilities using the deleted_at field when removal is necessary, preserving audit trails while preventing active display. The status field tracks maintenance progress through various lifecycle stages from 'scheduled' to 'completed' or 'cancelled'.

Administrators creating maintenance schedules must have appropriate permissions to schedule system maintenance. The operation automatically assigns the current administrator as the scheduling administrator and sets the initial status to 'scheduled'. Maintenance schedules can be created for various impact levels from low-impact maintenance requiring minimal downtime to critical maintenance affecting platform availability.

Related operations include viewing maintenance schedules via GET /maintenance-schedules/{id}, updating schedules via PUT /maintenance-schedules/{id}, and searching maintenance schedules via PATCH /maintenance-schedules. Administrators can also track maintenance execution progress and update actual timing information through subsequent operations.
operations.specification:
Validate that the requesting administrator has permission to create maintenance schedules. Check that scheduled_start_time is in the future and scheduled_end_time occurs after scheduled_start_time. Validate that estimated_duration_minutes matches the difference between scheduled start and end times. Ensure maintenance_type and impact_level values are from predefined valid options.

Create a new record in the discussion_board_maintenance_schedules table with the provided data. Set the scheduled_by_admin_id to the current authenticated administrator's ID. Set status to 'scheduled' and actual fields (actual_start_time, actual_end_time, actual_duration_minutes) to null since maintenance hasn't started yet. Set created_at and updated_at timestamps to current time.

Return the complete created maintenance schedule record including system-generated fields like ID and timestamps. Handle validation errors for required fields and data format issues. Ensure proper transaction handling for database operations.

requestBody.description: Maintenance schedule creation data including timing, description, and impact assessment

responseBody.description: Complete maintenance schedule record with system-generated fields

This operation returns the complete details of a single section including its name, description, status, display order, and administrative metadata. Sections are the primary organizational structure for categorizing articles and discussions on the platform.

The response includes information about which administrator created the section and when, as well as any modifications made to the section. This operation uses soft delete functionality, returning only active sections unless specifically filtered for archived content.

Section retrieval does not require any special permissions as sections are publicly viewable organizational structures, though only administrators can create or modify them.

Note: Sections marked as deleted via the deleted_at field will not be returned unless specifically queried for archived content.

operations.description:
Create a new discussion board section for organizing articles by topic.

This operation allows administrators to create new sections that serve as organizational categories for the discussion board platform. Each section represents a distinct topic area such as Politics, Economy, or Current Affairs, providing users with structured content browsing.

The operation validates that the requesting user has administrator privileges and ensures section name uniqueness across the platform (enforcing the @@unique([name]) database constraint). Upon successful creation, the section becomes immediately available for article posting and user browsing. The system automatically sets the section status to 'active' and records the creation timestamp and administrator identity for audit purposes.

Required fields from the database schema include name, description, display_order, and created_by_admin_id. The operation validates these requirements before creating the section record.

Related operations include PATCH /sections for listing sections, GET /sections/{sectionId} for retrieving specific section details, and PUT /sections/{sectionId} for updating section information.

operations.description:
Delete a discussion board section by performing a soft deletion operation.

This operation allows administrators to remove sections from the discussion board platform while preserving historical data. The deletion is implemented as a soft delete, meaning the section record remains in the database with a deleted_at timestamp rather than being permanently removed. This approach maintains data integrity and allows for potential restoration if needed.

Only users with administrator privileges can perform this operation. The system validates that the section exists and has not already been deleted before proceeding with the deletion. After successful deletion, the section will no longer appear in section lists or be available for new article creation, but existing articles within the section may be handled according to platform configuration (either preserved with section reference or reassigned to a default section).

The response includes the complete section information at the time of deletion, providing confirmation of the operation's success and a record of the deleted section's state. This information can be used for audit purposes or potential restoration workflows.

Related operations include creating sections (POST /sections), updating sections (PUT /sections/{sectionId}), and browsing sections (PATCH /sections). Administrators should also have access to view deleted sections through specialized administrative interfaces if restoration capabilities are implemented.

operations.description:
Permanently delete a discussion board section from the platform.

This operation allows super administrators to remove sections from the discussion board platform. The deletion is permanent and irreversible, completely removing the section record from the database. This action should be performed with caution as it cannot be undone.

Only users with super administrator privileges can perform this operation. The system validates that the section exists and has no dependent articles or comments before proceeding with deletion. If the section contains articles or comments, they must be handled according to platform configuration (either deleted along with the section or reassigned to a default section).

The response includes the complete section information that was deleted, providing confirmation of the operation's success. This information can be used for audit purposes but cannot be used for restoration since the deletion is permanent.

Related operations include creating sections (POST /sections), updating sections (PUT /sections/{sectionId}), and browsing sections (PATCH /sections). Super administrators should ensure proper backup procedures are in place before performing permanent deletions.

operations.specification:
Create a new ban record in the discussion_board_ban_records table with proper validation and administrator attribution.

Validation rules:
- ban_reason must be non-empty string
- ban_duration_days must be positive integer or null for permanent bans
- ban_status must be one of: 'active', 'expired', 'revoked'
- expires_at must be calculated based on ban_duration_days if provided

Implementation steps:
1. Validate request body fields against schema constraints
2. Calculate expires_at timestamp if ban_duration_days is provided
3. Create ban record in discussion_board_ban_records table
4. Create appropriate attribution record based on banning administrator type:
   - If banned by regular admin: create discussion_board_ban_record_of_admins record
   - If banned by super admin: create discussion_board_ban_record_of_super_admins record
5. Return complete ban record with created_at timestamp

Error handling:
- Return 400 for validation failures
- Return 404 if referenced administrator doesn't exist
- Return 403 if user lacks permission to ban

Security considerations:
- Only administrators can create ban records
- Validate administrator permissions before processing

operations.description:
Perform a comprehensive search across all articles in the discussion board platform.

This operation enables users to search for articles by title and content using full-text search capabilities. The search algorithm utilizes PostgreSQL's GIN indexes with trigram operations for efficient text matching, supporting fuzzy search and partial matching. Users can filter results by specific tags to narrow down search results to relevant content.

The search functionality implements pagination with configurable page sizes to handle large result sets efficiently. Results are sorted by relevance score based on search term matching, with fallback to chronological ordering when no search terms are provided. The operation supports complex search queries including phrase matching and boolean operators for advanced users.

Security considerations ensure that only published articles are included in search results, and user permissions are respected for content visibility. The search operation integrates with the discussion board's content moderation system to exclude inappropriate or flagged content from results.

Related operations include browsing articles by section (PATCH /articles) for section-specific content discovery and viewing individual articles (GET /articles/{articleId}) for detailed content access. This search operation serves as the primary content discovery mechanism for the entire platform.
operations.specification:
Query the discussion_board_articles table with full-text search capabilities using PostgreSQL GIN indexes on title and content fields. Implement text search using trigram operations (gin_trgm_ops) for fuzzy matching and partial word searches.

For tag filtering, join with discussion_board_article_tags table when tags are specified in the request. Apply tag filtering using AND logic when multiple tags are provided. Only include published articles (status = 'published') in search results.

Implement relevance scoring based on search term frequency and position in title vs content. Title matches should have higher weight than content matches. Use PostgreSQL's full-text search capabilities with ranking functions for optimal performance.

Apply pagination using cursor-based or offset-based approach depending on result set size. Include total count for pagination metadata. Sort results by relevance score when search terms are provided, otherwise sort by creation date (newest first).

Validate search parameters: ensure search text is sanitized to prevent injection attacks, validate tag names against allowed characters, enforce reasonable limits on pagination parameters. Return appropriate error responses for invalid search criteria.

requestBody.description: Search criteria including text search terms, tag filters, and pagination parameters

responseBody.description: Paginated list of article summaries matching the search criteria

operations.description:
Process an administrator promotion request review by approving or rejecting the request via creation of approval records.

This operation enables super administrators to review and decide on administrator promotion requests submitted by regular users. The review process involves evaluating the user's justification for seeking administrator status and making an informed decision based on platform governance policies.

When a promotion request is approved, the system creates an approval record linking to the promotion request and creates an administrator assignment for the user. Approved administrators gain privileges for content moderation, section management, and user banning capabilities while maintaining accountability through audit trails.

When a promotion request is rejected, the system creates a rejection record maintaining the decision details for compliance tracking. Rejected requests preserve records for future reference while the user remains a regular user.

The operation ensures proper audit trail maintenance by recording the reviewing administrator's identity, decision timestamp, and rationale in the approval records table. All review activities are logged for transparency and accountability in the administrator promotion process.

Security considerations require that only super administrators can access this operation, with proper authentication and authorization checks. The system validates that the promotion request exists and is in a pending state before processing the review.
operations.specification: Validate that the requesting user is authenticated as a super administrator with appropriate privileges. Check that the promotion request exists and has a status of 'pending'. Process the review decision by updating the promotion request status to 'approved' or 'rejected' based on the request body. If approved, create an administrator assignment record for the user and update their privileges. If rejected, maintain the request record with rejection details. Update timestamps and record the reviewing administrator's identity. Return the updated promotion request details with complete audit information.

parameters.name: requestId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the promotion request to review

requestBody.description: Review decision and optional notes for the promotion request

responseBody.description: Updated promotion request details with review decision

operations.specification: Verify the requesting user is a super administrator with proper authorization. Validate that the target administrator exists and is currently a regular administrator (not already a super admin). Update the administrator's grade from 'regular' to 'super' in the discussion_board_administrators table. Create a grade change record in discussion_board_administrator_grade_changes with the promotion details. Update the admin_id and super_admin_id references appropriately. Return the updated administrator information including the new grade level. Ensure the operation cannot demote the current user (self-demotion prevention).
operations.description:
Promote a regular administrator to super administrator status.

This administrative operation elevates a regular administrator's privileges to the highest level in the system, granting them additional capabilities including the ability to promote other administrators and manage system-wide settings. The operation requires the requesting user to be a super administrator and validates that the target administrator is currently at the regular grade level.

The promotion process updates the administrator's grade field in the discussion_board_administrators table and creates an audit trail entry in the discussion_board_administrator_grade_changes table. This ensures proper tracking of all grade transitions within the administrator hierarchy system. Super administrators cannot demote themselves through this operation, maintaining system integrity.

This operation is part of the comprehensive administrator management system that supports the hierarchical governance structure. After promotion, the administrator gains access to all super administrator capabilities including promotion request review, administrator grade management, and system-wide configuration access.

parameters.name: administratorId
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the regular administrator to be promoted

responseBody.description: Updated administrator information after successful promotion

operations.name: promote

operations.specification: Validate that the requesting user is a super administrator. Verify the target administrator exists and is currently a super administrator. Ensure the requesting administrator is not attempting to demote themselves. Create a grade change record in discussion_board_administrator_grade_changes table with old grade 'super', new grade 'regular', and the provided reason. Update the target administrator's grade to 'regular' in discussion_board_administrators table. Update the grade_changed_at timestamp. Return the updated administrator record.
operations.description:
This operation allows a super administrator to demote another super administrator to regular administrator grade.

The demotion process maintains comprehensive audit trails by recording the grade change in the administrator grade changes table. This ensures accountability and transparency in administrator management operations.

Only super administrators can perform this operation, and they cannot demote themselves as a system protection measure. The operation requires a reason for the demotion to document the decision-making process.

After successful demotion, the affected administrator loses super administrator privileges but retains regular administrator capabilities. The operation preserves all existing administrator assignments and relationships while updating the grade level.

This operation is part of the hierarchical administrator management system that supports platform governance and security by enabling controlled privilege escalation and de-escalation processes.

parameters.name: administratorId

operations.description:
Assign capabilities to a specific administrator with defined permission levels.

This operation allows super administrators to grant specific administrative privileges to target administrators. Capabilities define what administrative functions an administrator can perform, such as content moderation, user management, section administration, or system configuration. Each capability is assigned with a specific permission level that determines the scope of allowed actions.

The assignment process validates that the requesting user has super administrator privileges and that the target administrator exists in the system. Each capability type and permission level is verified against the system's allowed configuration. The operation supports assigning multiple capabilities in a single request and handles both new assignments and updates to existing capability permissions.

Successful assignment returns the complete updated list of capabilities for the administrator, providing immediate visibility into the granted privileges. This operation is essential for maintaining the hierarchical administrator system and ensuring proper access control across the discussion board platform.

operations.description:
Revoke a specific administrative capability assignment from an administrator.

This operation allows super administrators to remove specific capabilities from administrators while maintaining an audit trail. The revocation is performed through soft deletion by setting the deleted_at timestamp, preserving the historical record of when the capability was assigned and revoked.

When a capability is revoked, the administrator immediately loses access to the associated permissions. The capability record remains in the database with a revocation timestamp for compliance and audit purposes. This operation requires super administrator privileges and should only be used when administrators no longer require specific permissions or when permissions need adjustment based on role changes.

The operation ensures that capability revocation is properly tracked and can be audited later. All capability assignments and revocations are timestamped for complete accountability. Authorization checks verify that only super administrators can perform this action, preventing unauthorized capability modifications.

operations.description:
Review a ban appeal by updating its status and providing a decision reason.

This operation allows administrators to process ban appeals submitted by users. The appeal review workflow involves evaluating the user's appeal reason against the original ban decision and making a determination to either approve (overturn the ban) or reject (uphold the ban) the appeal. The operation references the discussion_board_ban_appeals table structure including the status workflow, decision_reason field, and soft deletion tracking via deleted_at.

Administrators must have appropriate moderation privileges to perform this action. The appeal must be in a reviewable state (pending or under_review status with deleted_at null) to be eligible for review. Once reviewed, the appeal status becomes final and cannot be changed again, though the record may be soft deleted if needed.

The operation validates that the specified ban record and appeal exist and are properly linked. It ensures the reviewing administrator is authorized and records the decision timestamp for audit trail purposes. The appeal workflow supports status transitions between pending, under_review, approved, and rejected states as defined in the database schema.

Related operations include viewing ban appeals lists and accessing individual ban records for context during the review process.

operations.description:
Retrieve comprehensive ban statistics and analytics with advanced filtering capabilities for administrator review and moderation analysis.

This operation provides administrators with detailed insights into ban patterns, moderation effectiveness, and user management trends across the discussion board platform. The analytics include ban statistics by status, duration type, time periods, appeal outcomes, and administrator performance metrics.

Administrators can filter results by ban status (active, expired, revoked, appealed), ban duration type (temporary, permanent), specific time ranges, appeal status, and the administrator who issued the bans. The system supports complex filtering combinations to generate targeted analytics reports for moderation review and platform governance.

The response includes paginated ban summary data optimized for analytics display, providing essential information without overwhelming administrators with excessive detail. Each ban record summary includes key metrics and status information suitable for trend analysis and moderation decision-making.

This operation requires administrator privileges as it accesses sensitive moderation data and ban statistics. The analytics support compliance reporting, moderation effectiveness assessment, and platform governance oversight by providing comprehensive visibility into ban enforcement patterns and outcomes.

Security considerations include proper access control verification and audit logging of all analytics queries to maintain accountability and prevent unauthorized access to moderation data.
operations.specification:
Query the discussion_board_user_bans table with comprehensive filtering capabilities for ban analytics. Implement pagination using cursor-based or offset-based approach depending on performance requirements.

Apply filters based on request parameters: ban_status (active, expired, revoked, appealed), ban_duration_type (temporary, permanent), date ranges (ban_started_at, ban_ends_at), appeal_status (none, pending, under_review, approved, rejected), and banning_administrator_id.

Join with discussion_board_admins table to include administrator information in results. Calculate aggregate statistics including total bans, active bans, expired bans, appeal rates, and average ban duration.

Implement efficient database queries with proper indexing on ban_status, ban_started_at, banning_administrator_id, and appeal_status fields. Use database aggregation functions for statistical calculations to minimize application-level processing.

Include comprehensive error handling for invalid filter parameters and ensure proper authorization checks verify administrator privileges before processing analytics requests. Log all analytics queries for audit purposes.

Optimize response structure for analytics consumption, including summary statistics alongside paginated ban records. Consider implementing caching for frequently requested analytics patterns to improve performance.

requestBody.description: Ban analytics filtering criteria including status filters, time ranges, and statistical parameters

responseBody.description: Paginated ban analytics results with summary statistics and ban record summaries

current.description:
Current page number being viewed (1-indexed).

Indicates which page of results is currently being returned. Page
numbering starts from 1, so the first page is page 1 (not 0). This value
reflects the page parameter from the request after validation and bounds
checking.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records per page.

Defines the upper bound on how many records can be returned in a single
page. This corresponds to the limit parameter from the request. The
actual number of records in the data array may be less than this value on
the final page or when total records are fewer than the limit.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Maximum records per page. Actual count may be less on last page.

records.description:
Total count of all records matching the query criteria.

Represents the complete number of records available across all pages, not
just the current page. This value is computed via a COUNT query and is
essential for calculating total pages and displaying pagination UI
elements like "Showing 1-10 of 150 results".
records.x-autobe-specification: Total record count across all pages.

pages.description:
Total number of pages available.

Calculated as ceiling of {@link records} divided by {@link limit}. When
records is 0, pages will also be 0. This value enables clients to render
page navigation controls and validate page bounds.
pages.x-autobe-specification: Total pages. Calculated as Math.ceil(records / limit).

IPage.IPagination.description:
Pagination metadata containing current page position and total data
statistics.

This interface provides comprehensive pagination information returned
alongside paginated list data. It enables clients to implement navigation
controls, display progress indicators, and determine data boundaries for UI
rendering.
IPage.IPagination.x-autobe-specification: Pagination metadata for paginated list responses. Included in all list endpoint responses.

access.description:
Short-lived JWT access token for authenticating API requests.

This token must be included in the Authorization header using the Bearer
scheme (e.g., `Authorization: Bearer {access}`) for all endpoints requiring
authentication. The token contains encoded claims including user identity,
roles, and permissions. Typically expires within 15-60 minutes for
security; use the refresh token to obtain a new access token when expired.
access.x-autobe-specification: JWT access token. Use in Authorization header as "Bearer {access}".

refresh.description:
Long-lived refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

Used to request new access tokens when the current access token expires,
allowing session continuation without re-authentication. Should be stored
securely and transmitted only to the token refresh endpoint. Typical
lifetime ranges from 7 to 30 days depending on security requirements.
refresh.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens without re-authentication.

expired_at.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp when the access token expires.

After this timestamp, the access token will be rejected by authenticated
endpoints. Clients should proactively refresh before expiration to maintain
seamless user experience. A common strategy is to refresh when remaining
time falls below 5 minutes. This timestamp is also embedded within the JWT
itself as the "exp" claim.
expired_at.x-autobe-specification: Access token expiration timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

refreshable_until.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp indicating the absolute session expiration deadline.

Represents the latest possible time the refresh token can be used. Once
this timestamp is reached, the user must fully re-authenticate with
credentials. This defines the maximum session duration regardless of
activity. If refresh token rotation is enabled, this deadline may extend
with each successful refresh.
refreshable_until.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token expiration timestamp. Re-authentication required after this time.

IAuthorizationToken.description:
JWT-based authorization token pair with expiration metadata.

Provides a complete authentication token structure containing both access and
refresh tokens along with their respective expiration timestamps. This
dual-token pattern enables secure, stateless authentication with automatic
session renewal capabilities.

The access token is short-lived for security, while the refresh token allows
obtaining new access tokens without requiring the user to re-enter
credentials. This structure is automatically included in authentication
responses across all generated backend applications.
IAuthorizationToken.x-autobe-specification: Dual-token authentication structure with access/refresh tokens and expiration info.

email.description: User's email address used for authentication and platform communication. Must be a valid email format and unique across all accounts.
email.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_users.email column. Must be unique across all user accounts. Validated for email format compliance before storage.

password.description: User's password for account authentication. Will be securely hashed before storage. Minimum 8 characters required.
password.x-autobe-specification: Plain text password provided by user that will be hashed using secure algorithms before storage in password_hash column. Minimum 8 characters required for security compliance.

display_name.description: Public display name shown on user profiles and alongside user-generated content. Must be at least 1 character long.
display_name.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_users.display_name column. Minimum 1 character required. Used as public display name across the platform.

bio.description: Optional biography text describing the user's background, interests, or expertise. Can be left empty.
bio.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_users.bio column. Optional field that accepts null values. Used for user biography/description text.

IDiscussionBoardUser.IJoin.description: User registration request containing essential information for creating a new account on the discussion board platform. Validates email format, password strength, and display name requirements before creating the user record.
IDiscussionBoardUser.IJoin.x-autobe-specification: User registration request mapping directly to discussion_board_users table fields. Email and display_name map directly to database columns. Password is provided as plain text and requires backend hashing before storage. Bio is optional and accepts null values. This DTO excludes auto-generated fields (id, password_hash, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) which are handled by the backend during user creation.

id.description: Unique identifier for the password reset request.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_user_password_resets.id. UUID primary key that uniquely identifies the password reset record.

token.description: Unique reset token used for password recovery authentication.
token.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_user_password_resets.token. Unique token generated for password recovery that is sent to the user's email.

expired_at.description: Expiration timestamp when the reset token becomes invalid.
expired_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_user_password_resets.expired_at. Timestamp indicating when the reset token becomes invalid and cannot be used for password recovery.

used_at.description: Timestamp when the reset token was successfully used, or null if still available.
used_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_user_password_resets.used_at. Nullable timestamp indicating when the reset token was successfully used to change a password. Null means the token is still available for use.

created_at.description: Creation timestamp of the password reset request.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_user_password_resets.created_at. Timestamp when the password reset request was initially created.

updated_at.description: Last update timestamp of the password reset record.
updated_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_user_password_resets.updated_at. Timestamp when the password reset record was last updated, typically when used_at gets populated.

deleted_at.description: Deletion timestamp for soft-deleted reset records, or null if active.
deleted_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_user_password_resets.deleted_at. Nullable timestamp indicating when the reset record was soft-deleted for security purposes.

user.description: User account associated with this password reset request.
user.x-autobe-specification: Join from discussion_board_user_password_resets.discussion_board_user_id to discussion_board_users.id. Returns ISummary for user reference.

actor_type.description: Actor type associated with this password reset request.
actor_type.x-autobe-specification: Computed property based on user relation. Always returns 'user' since this schema maps to discussion_board_user_password_resets table which only contains user password resets.

IDiscussionBoardUserPasswordReset.description: Comprehensive password reset information including token status, validity period, and associated actor type details. This DTO represents the unified view of password reset requests across all actor types (user, administrator, super administrator) in the discussion board platform.
IDiscussionBoardUserPasswordReset.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_user_password_resets table for core fields. The actor_type property is computed based on which password reset table the record originates from (discussion_board_user_password_resets, discussion_board_admin_password_resets, or discussion_board_super_admin_password_resets). This unified view allows administrators to verify reset status across all actor types.

IDiscussionBoardUserSession.ISummary.description: Summary information for user sessions used in administrative session management and monitoring. Provides essential session metadata including connection information, timestamps, and user context while excluding sensitive authentication tokens.
IDiscussionBoardUserSession.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping: id, ip, user_agent, referrer, created_at, expired_at, last_accessed_at. Relation: user via JOIN to discussion_board_users for display_name. Excluded: access_token, refresh_token (security), discussion_board_user_id (replaced with user object).

IDiscussionBoardSystemConfiguration.description: Complete system configuration entity containing all configuration details and metadata. This DTO provides administrative access to system configuration parameters including key, value, data type, description, category, sensitivity flag, and lifecycle timestamps. Sensitive configuration values are exposed in plain text since this is an administrative endpoint requiring proper authentication.
IDiscussionBoardSystemConfiguration.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_system_configurations table. Fields: id (UUID primary key), config_key (unique configuration identifier), config_value (configuration value string), data_type (value type specification), description (human-readable explanation), category (functional grouping), is_sensitive (security masking flag), created_at (creation timestamp), updated_at (modification timestamp), deleted_at (soft deletion timestamp, nullable).

config_key.description: Unique identifier for the configuration parameter. Used to reference the configuration in code and administration interfaces.
config_key.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_system_configurations.config_key column. Must be unique across all configuration entries. Validated for uniqueness before creation.

config_value.description: The actual value of the configuration parameter stored as a string for flexibility.
config_value.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_system_configurations.config_value column. Stores the actual configuration value as a string for flexibility across different data types.

data_type.description: The data type of the configuration value (e.g., 'string', 'integer', 'boolean', 'json').
data_type.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_system_configurations.data_type column. Specifies the expected data type for the config_value (e.g., 'string', 'integer', 'boolean', 'json').

description.description: Human-readable description explaining the purpose and usage of this configuration parameter.
description.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_system_configurations.description column. Provides human-readable explanation of the configuration parameter's purpose and usage.

category.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_system_configurations.category column. Groups related configurations by functional area (e.g., 'authentication', 'content', 'performance', 'security').

is_sensitive.description: Indicates whether this configuration contains sensitive information that should be masked in logs and UI displays.
is_sensitive.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_system_configurations.is_sensitive column. Determines whether the configuration value should be masked in logs and UI displays for security purposes.

IDiscussionBoardSystemConfiguration.ICre.description: Request body for creating new system configuration parameters in the discussion board platform. Contains the configuration key, value, data type specification, descriptive explanation, functional category, and sensitivity flag. Used to add new configurable platform settings that control behavior, features, and operational parameters.
IDiscussionBoardSystemConfiguration.ICre.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_system_configurations table for creation operations. Excludes system-generated fields: id (auto UUID), created_at/updated_at (auto timestamps), deleted_at (soft delete). Validates config_key uniqueness and ensures all required fields are provided with appropriate data type constraints.

refresh_token.description: JWT refresh token for authentication renewal
refresh_token.x-autobe-specification: JWT refresh token retrieved from discussion_board_admin_sessions table. Used to validate the administrator's session and generate new access and refresh tokens. The token must be valid, not expired, and associated with an active administrator session.

IDiscussionBoardAdmin.IRefresh.description: Request body for refreshing administrator authentication tokens. Contains the refresh token needed to validate the session and generate new authentication credentials.
IDiscussionBoardAdmin.IRefresh.x-autobe-specification: This DTO represents the refresh token submission for administrator authentication renewal. The refresh_token field contains the JWT refresh token that will be validated against active sessions in the discussion_board_admin_sessions table. If valid, the system generates new access and refresh tokens and returns them in the response.

refresh_token.description: Valid refresh token obtained from previous authentication session

IDiscussionBoardUser.IRefresh.description: Request body for refreshing user authentication tokens. Contains the refresh token obtained from a previous authentication session.
IDiscussionBoardUser.IRefresh.x-autobe-specification: Maps to refresh_token column in discussion_board_user_sessions table. The refresh token is validated against stored session records to ensure it hasn't expired or been revoked.

IDiscussionBoardSuperAdmin.IRefresh.description: Request body for refreshing super administrator authentication tokens. Contains the refresh token that will be validated against active sessions to generate new access tokens with updated expiration.
IDiscussionBoardSuperAdmin.IRefresh.x-autobe-specification: Maps to the refresh token validation process. The refresh token is validated against active super admin sessions to ensure it's valid and unexpired before issuing new access tokens.

IDiscussionBoardAdmin.ILogin.description: Request body containing administrator login credentials for authentication.
IDiscussionBoardAdmin.ILogin.x-autobe-specification: Maps directly to email and password fields. Backend will hash the provided password and compare against stored password_hash. Email must be validated against unique constraint.

email.description: Unique email address for super administrator authentication and communication.
email.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from request email to discussion_board_super_admins.email column. Must be validated for email format uniqueness before account creation.

password.description: Password for super administrator authentication. Will be securely hashed before storage.
password.x-autobe-specification: Plain text password from request that will be securely hashed before storage in discussion_board_super_admins.password_hash column. Must meet minimum security requirements.

privilege_level.description: Privilege level indicator for super administrator capabilities and access permissions.
privilege_level.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from request privilege_level to discussion_board_super_admins.privilege_level column. Defines the administrative capabilities and access levels for the super administrator.

IDiscussionBoardSuperAdmin.IJoin.description: Request body for super administrator registration containing authentication credentials and privilege information required to create a new super administrator account.
IDiscussionBoardSuperAdmin.IJoin.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from super administrator registration request to discussion_board_super_admins table. Email and privilege_level map directly to database columns. Password is hashed before storage using secure algorithms. All fields are required for account creation.

IDiscussionBoardSuperAdmin.ILogin.description: Authentication credentials for super administrator login. Contains the email address and password required to verify super administrator identity and grant access to administrative functions.
IDiscussionBoardSuperAdmin.ILogin.x-autobe-specification: Maps: email directly from database. Transforms: password_hash field becomes plain password field for authentication input. Excluded: id (auto), privilege_level (from account), timestamps (auto).

id.description: Unique identifier for the super administrator account.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_super_admins.id column. Primary key UUID that uniquely identifies each super administrator account.

email.description: Email address associated with the super administrator account for authentication and communication purposes.
email.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_super_admins.email column. Unique email address used for super administrator authentication and system communication.

privilege_level.description: Privilege level indicating the administrative capabilities and access permissions for this super administrator account.

IDiscussionBoardSuperAdmin.x-autobe-specification:
Aggregated dashboard statistics computed from multiple database tables:
- Total users: COUNT(*) from discussion_board_users WHERE deleted_at IS NULL
- Total articles: COUNT(*) from discussion_board_articles WHERE deleted_at IS NULL
- Total comments: COUNT(*) from discussion_board_comments WHERE deleted_at IS NULL
- Section statistics: JOIN discussion_board_sections with discussion_board_section_statistics
- Recent activities: SELECT * from discussion_board_system_activities ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 10
- Engagement rate: (total_comments / total_articles) * 100, with edge case handling for zero articles
- Platform health: Calculated based on error rates, performance metrics, and system uptime indicators

Complete file attachment metadata record including file properties, storage information, and usage statistics.

This schema represents the comprehensive metadata for files attached to discussion board articles. It includes technical details like file type and size, storage path for retrieval, upload tracking information, and download statistics for analytics. The record maintains full lifecycle tracking with creation, update, and deletion timestamps.

File attachments support various formats including documents, PDFs, and other supported file types. Each file maintains its original name, MIME type identification, and descriptive information provided by the uploader. The storage path enables secure file access while download tracking provides usage analytics for content management.

The schema follows the discussion_board_article_files database structure, ensuring data consistency across file management operations.

start.description: Start timestamp for the date range (inclusive). Records with timestamps on or after this value will be included.
start.x-autobe-specification: Optional start timestamp for filtering records. When provided, filters records with timestamps on or after this value. Implementation should use >= comparison when only start is provided, or BETWEEN clause when both start and end are provided.

end.description: End timestamp for the date range (inclusive). Records with timestamps on or before this value will be included.
end.x-autobe-specification: Optional end timestamp for filtering records. When provided, filters records with timestamps on or before this value. Implementation should use <= comparison when only end is provided, or BETWEEN clause when both start and end are provided.

IDiscussionBoardDateRange.description: Date range specification for filtering records by timestamp boundaries. Supports flexible date range queries with optional start and end timestamps.
IDiscussionBoardDateRange.x-autobe-specification: Utility type for date range filtering operations. Start and end timestamps are optional to support various filtering scenarios: start-only (records after start date), end-only (records before end date), or both (records between start and end dates). When both are provided, implementation should use BETWEEN clause; when only one is provided, use appropriate inequality comparison.
